label: End-of-episode D1 ramp after the previous trial reached S2, strongest after a1->S2 (rare)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.1% of steps) that fires only at D1 in the last ~12 trials of the episode. Its size grows faster than linearly with the episode trial past about 85, and only when the previous trial reached S2. It is largest after a1->S2 (rare transition) and smaller after a2->S2 (common). After an S2 visit it is also higher when the ideal-observer belief favours S1 (positive belief_lo), i.e. when reaching S2 was unexpected or bad. Previous reward adds little (scored, small negative). It is zero at GO and D2. Timing alone gives R^2 0.15; these 6 observed-only terms give dev 0.716 and test 0.722 R^2 beyond timing, far above the profile additive ceiling (all 0.11, all observed 0.09), because the effect is an episode-time x last-state interaction. Without the model outputs nothing is lost: the earlier policy-decile cue scored only 0.04 on its own, and belief_lo adds about 0.03 here.

issues: The score reproduces: the 6 terms give a test R^2 beyond timing of 0.722. The claims 'D1 only', 'last ~12 trials' and 'after S2' hold. The timing baseline is zero at GO and D2 and nonzero only from D1 decile 7 on, and residuals at GO and D2 are +0.

The superlinear growth is misattributed. A single linear term, (phase==D1)*max(ep_trial-85,0)*a1->S2, gets test 0.599 by itself. Adding a squared ramp for a1->S2 gets a weight of about 0 (8e-05). The faster-than-linear growth belongs to a2->S2 (common): that quadratic weight is 0.0113, test 0.724 with 5 terms. 'Grows faster than linearly' should not be stated generally, and the a1->S2 ramp is linear.

The a2->S2 description is misleading. A linear a2->S2 ramp alone gets weight 0.0007, essentially zero. The a2->S2 response is late-onset (quadratic), and it depends on belief_lo (weight 0.031) and on the previous reward.

The belief effect is specific to a2->S2. belief_lo*ramp gets weight 0.016 to 0.031 on a2->S2 and 0.002 on a1->S2. The claim that after any S2 visit it is higher when belief favours S1 is only true for common a2->S2 visits.

'The previous reward matters little' is wrong for a2->S2. A rewarded a2->S2 term gets weight 0.088 per ramp unit, comparable in size to the base a2 slope, and it adds about 0.02 test R^2. For a1->S2 the reward weight is about 0 (0.002), so there the claim holds.

The worst misses are high D1 activations on the window's first trial, where prev_state is unknown (-1). This is a window-truncation limit, not an explanatory gap: a ramp*(prev_state==-1) term helps only slightly. Otherwise, the misses run with the original terms show small systematic errors: D1 after a1 S2 r is under-predicted by 0.044, and S1 histories are over-predicted by about 0.015.
skeptic.revised_label: Late-episode D1 ramp after reaching S2. After a1->S2 (rare) it is a strong linear ramp that does not depend on reward. After a2->S2 (common) it is weaker, sets in late (quadratic), and is raised by a previous reward and by belief that S1 is good.
